title: Monster
author: Walter Dean Myers
awards: National Book Award finalist 1999 · Edgar YA nominee 2000 · Printz winner 2000
maturity_note: A store owner is shot in a robbery; rape in jail is implied, and a teen mentions getting a girl pregnant. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Sixteen-year-old Steve Harmon is on trial for murder, accused of being the lookout in a robbery that went wrong. He tells the story as a movie script he writes in his cell. You have to decide for yourself what he did.

title: Speak
author: Laurie Halse Anderson
awards: National Book Award finalist 1999 · Edgar YA nominee 2000 · Printz honor 2000
maturity_note: A rape at a party, described briefly but clearly; self-harm (cutting); depression and isolation. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Melinda starts high school as an outcast because she called the police at a summer party, and now she has almost stopped talking. Bit by bit, and mostly through art class, she lets you know what really happened that night.

title: The House of the Scorpion
author: Nancy Farmer
awards: National Book Award winner 2002 · Newbery honor 2003 · Printz honor 2003
maturity_note: Drug-lord violence, child labor camps and a few deaths; nothing graphic. Common Sense Media: 11+.
description: Matt is a clone of El Patrón, a 140-year-old drug lord who rules a country between the U.S. and Mexico. Most clones are treated like animals, but Matt is raised in luxury, and he slowly works out why.

title: A Northern Light
author: Jennifer Donnelly
maturity_note: A drowned young woman, a pregnancy and a murder; frank talk about sex and marriage. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: It's 1906, and Mattie works at a lakeside hotel in the Adirondacks to save for college. A guest drowns, and Mattie is holding a bundle of letters the dead woman asked her to burn. Based on a real murder case.

title: Airborn
author: Kenneth Oppel
maturity_note: Sky pirates and some fights; nothing graphic. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Matt Cruse is a cabin boy on a luxury airship who once rescued a dying balloonist with stories of strange winged creatures. A year later the balloonist's granddaughter comes aboard to find out if they're real, just before pirates attack.

title: Looking for Alaska
author: John Green
maturity_note: Lots of sex talk and some sex (including oral sex and porn), heavy drinking and smoking, drunk driving, and a sudden death that may be a suicide. Common Sense Media: 16+.
description: Miles leaves home for an Alabama boarding school looking for a "Great Perhaps" and finds Alaska Young, who is brilliant, funny and self-destructive. The book counts down to something that changes everything, then counts up from it.

title: I Am the Messenger
author: Markus Zusak
maturity_note: Strong language, a husband who rapes his wife, an attempted rape that is stopped, bloody beatings and sexual talk. Common Sense Media: 15+.
description: Ed Kennedy is a 19-year-old cab driver going nowhere until he accidentally stops a bank robbery. Then playing cards start arriving in the mail with addresses and times on them. Someone is sending him on missions, and he has to figure out who.

title: American Born Chinese
author: Gene Luen Yang
awards: National Book Award finalist 2006 · Printz winner 2007
maturity_note: Racist stereotypes shown on purpose so the book can take them apart; schoolyard bullying. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Three stories that seem unrelated: the Monkey King who wants to be a god, Jin Wang who just wants to fit in at a new school, and an all-American teenager whose embarrassing cousin visits every year. They come together in a way you won't see coming.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
maturity_note: Nazi Germany: bombings, beatings, death-camp imagery, a suicide, and the deaths of major characters; antisemitic slurs. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Death narrates the story of Liesel, a girl in Nazi Germany who steals books and learns to read with her foster father. The family hides a Jewish man in their basement. Long, and it will break your heart.

title: The White Darkness
author: Geraldine McCaughrean
maturity_note: Several murders, by poison and explosion; a teen girl brags about a relationship with a 30-year-old man; an adult manipulates and endangers the narrator. Common Sense Media: 15+.
description: Fourteen-year-old Sym's closest companion is the imaginary ghost of a dead Antarctic explorer. When her late father's friend, whom she calls Uncle, takes her on a trip to Antarctica, it turns out he has an obsession of his own, and she may not get home.

title: Jellicoe Road
author: Melina Marchetta
maturity_note: Suicide, drinking, a crash that killed several parents, and some sexual content. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Taylor leads her boarding school's side in a secret territory war with the town kids and a visiting army cadet troop. Then the woman who took her in disappears, leaving behind a manuscript about five kids eighteen years earlier. Confusing at first; it pays off.

title: The Disreputable History of Frankie Landau-Banks
author: E. Lockhart
awards: National Book Award finalist 2008 · Printz honor 2009
maturity_note: Some drinking at parties; mostly pranks and power plays. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: At her elite boarding school, Frankie's boyfriend belongs to a secret all-male society that won't let her in. So she starts running it from the shadows, through a series of increasingly ambitious pranks. By the author of We Were Liars.

title: Nation
author: Terry Pratchett
maturity_note: A tsunami kills a whole village; a few later deaths. Common Sense Media: 11+.
description: A tsunami wipes out Mau's island village while he's away, and the only other survivor is an English girl from a shipwreck. Together they start building a new nation, and Mau starts questioning his gods. Funny, wise, and very Pratchett.

title: Ship Breaker
author: Paolo Bacigalupi
awards: National Book Award finalist 2010 · Printz winner 2011
maturity_note: Violence, and an abusive father who is addicted to drugs. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: In a future Gulf Coast drowned by rising seas, Nailer scavenges copper from wrecked oil tankers. After a hurricane he finds a wrecked clipper ship with a rich girl still alive inside, and he has to decide whether to save her or strip the ship.

title: Revolver
author: Marcus Sedgwick
maturity_note: A frozen body and a menacing stranger with a gun; tense rather than graphic. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Arctic Sweden, 1910. Sig is alone in a cabin with his father's frozen body when a stranger arrives claiming his father owed him gold. There's a revolver hidden in the storeroom. Short and very tense.

title: Stolen
author: Lucy Christopher
maturity_note: A girl is kidnapped and held in the desert; no sexual assault, but menace throughout. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Gemma is drugged at an airport and wakes up in the middle of the Australian outback with the man who took her. She tells the story as a letter to him. It gets more complicated than a kidnapping story usually does.

title: Where Things Come Back
author: John Corey Whaley
maturity_note: Frequent strong profanity, the narrator has sex with two young women, a cousin's heroin overdose, gory zombie dreams, and a suicide. Common Sense Media: 16+.
description: The summer Cullen's younger brother vanishes, his small Arkansas town is obsessed with a woodpecker everyone thought was extinct. A second, seemingly unrelated story about a young missionary slowly converges with his. Won both the Printz and the Morris.

title: The Scorpio Races
author: Maggie Stiefvater
maturity_note: Killer water horses; riders die, some violently. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Every November on the island of Thisby, riders race deadly water horses that rise from the sea, and some don't survive. Sean is the reigning champion. Puck is the first girl to enter, and she's racing to save her family's home.

title: Jasper Jones
author: Craig Silvey
maturity_note: Constant profanity, a girl's body found hanging, racism and child abuse. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: In a small Australian town in 1965, the town outcast knocks on 13-year-old Charlie's window and shows him a girl's body in the bush. They hide it and try to find out who killed her before the town blames Jasper. Australia's answer to To Kill a Mockingbird.

title: Code Name Verity
author: Elizabeth Wein
maturity_note: Gestapo torture described, wartime deaths, heavy profanity, and unwanted advances toward women. Common Sense Media: 15+.
description: A British spy captured in Nazi-occupied France makes a deal: she'll write out everything she knows, and she uses it to tell the story of her best friend, a pilot. Then the second half of the book makes you reread the first.

title: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
author: Benjamin Alire Sáenz
maturity_note: Some swearing, drinking and drugs, and a violent hate crime. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: El Paso, 1987. Ari is angry and lonely until he meets Dante at the swimming pool, a boy who knows how to swim and how to talk about anything. A quiet book about friendship, family and figuring out who you are.

title: Midwinterblood
author: Marcus Sedgwick
maturity_note: Ritual sacrifice and some very bloody deaths (a man is stabbed and cut open); a reference to adultery. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Seven linked stories travel back in time on a Scandinavian island where nobody seems to age. Each one is about the same two people, meeting again. By the end you see how it all started.

title: Maggot Moon
author: Sally Gardner
maturity_note: Brutal regime violence, including a beating and a killing. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Standish can't read or write and lives under a 1950s dictatorship that is about to land a man on the moon. He and his only friend stumble on what the government is hiding. Very short chapters.

title: Bone Gap
author: Laura Ruby
awards: National Book Award finalist 2015 · Printz winner 2016
maturity_note: An implied rape and an attempt to force a girl into oral sex, a teen sex scene, a woman held captive, and a severe beating and stabbing. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: In the town of Bone Gap, Roza vanished, and Finn is the only one who saw her taken. Nobody believes him, because he can't describe the man's face. Part mystery, part fairy tale.

title: Scythe
author: Neal Shusterman
maturity_note: Many killings, some described, including mass killings and messy suicides. It's the premise of the book. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: Nobody dies anymore, so Scythes are appointed to kill people to keep the population in check. Two teenagers are made apprentices against their will, and only one will be chosen. The other may be the winner's first job.

title: The Sun Is Also a Star
author: Nicola Yoon
awards: National Book Award finalist 2016 · Printz honor 2017
maturity_note: Some swearing and a little sexual content. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Natasha is being deported to Jamaica tonight. Daniel is a poet who is supposed to become a doctor. They meet in New York on Natasha's last day, and the strangers they pass get chapters of their own.

title: Long Way Down
author: Jason Reynolds
awards: Edgar YA winner 2018 · Newbery honor 2018 · Printz honor 2018
maturity_note: A brother shot dead, a gun, and the pull of revenge; little else. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: Will's brother has been shot, and Will knows the rules: don't cry, don't snitch, get revenge. He takes the gun and gets in the elevator, and on every floor someone from his past gets on. Told in verse over sixty seconds.

title: The Hate U Give
author: Angie Thomas
awards: Edgar YA nominee 2018 · Morris winner 2018 · Printz honor 2018
maturity_note: Heavy swearing, a police shooting, drug dealing and gang violence. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Starr lives in a poor neighborhood and goes to a rich prep school, and she keeps the two worlds apart. Then she's the only witness when a police officer shoots her unarmed childhood friend. What she says could change everything, and put her in danger.

title: Strange the Dreamer
author: Laini Taylor
maturity_note: A backstory of abducted girls who were raped and forced to bear children, slaughtered babies, and a sex scene with some detail. Common Sense Media: 15+.
description: Lazlo Strange is a junior librarian obsessed with a lost city whose name was erased from everyone's memory. When a warrior from that city comes looking for help, Lazlo goes along. Something is living in the floating citadel above it.

title: The Poet X
author: Elizabeth Acevedo
awards: National Book Award winner 2018 · Carnegie winner 2019 · Printz winner 2019
maturity_note: Her mother hits her and makes her kneel on rice; a heavy-petting scene, groping, and frank talk about sex and bodies. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Xiomara lives in Harlem with a strict religious mother and pours everything she can't say into a notebook of poems. Then she's invited to join the school's slam poetry club. Told in verse.

title: I, Claudia
author: Mary McCoy
maturity_note: A death, scandals and cruelty among students; mild language. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Claudia narrates how she rose to the top of her elite private school's student government, through scandal, betrayal and at least one suspicious death. The plot borrows from the Roman emperors, and it's ruthless.

title: Where the World Ends
author: Geraldine McCaughrean
maturity_note: Starvation, deaths, and boys turning on each other. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: It's 1727, and a group of boys and men are left on a sea rock off Scotland to hunt seabirds for a few weeks. Nobody comes back for them. Based on a true story.

title: Everything Sad Is Untrue
author: Daniel Nayeri
maturity_note: Children watch their mother being beaten, a very bloody bull slaughter, a boy is whipped, and a classmate stabs other kids. Common Sense Media: 11+.
description: Twelve-year-old Daniel is an Iranian refugee in Oklahoma, and his classmates don't believe a word he says. So he tells them everything, in the style of the Thousand and One Nights, about his family, his escape and who he used to be. Mostly true.

title: Firekeeper's Daughter
author: Angeline Boulley
awards: Edgar YA winner 2022 · Morris winner 2022 · Printz winner 2022
maturity_note: Meth addiction, murders and a suicide by gun, constant crude language, a lot of casual sex, and a rape of a teen by an adult (not detailed). Common Sense Media: 15+.
description: Daunis is half Ojibwe and about to start college when she witnesses a murder. Now she's working undercover with the FBI to find who is spreading a dangerous new drug on her reservation. A thriller written by an Ojibwe author.

title: Graceling
author: Kristin Cashore
maturity_note: Fighting and some brutality; a sex scene that isn't graphic. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: In Katsa's world, a few people are born Graced with an extreme skill. Hers is killing, and her uncle the king uses her as his enforcer. Then she meets a prince investigating a strange kidnapping.

title: Seraphina
author: Rachel Hartman
maturity_note: A murder, and dragons who can be frightening. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: Dragons can take human form, and an uneasy peace with humans is about to hit its fortieth year. Seraphina is the court musician, and she's hiding that she's half dragon. Then a prince is murdered in a way that looks like a dragon did it.

title: Between Shades of Gray
author: Ruta Sepetys
maturity_note: Labor-camp cruelty, starvation and corpses; Lina is groped in a shower line, and a mother is forced into prostitution to save her son. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: It's 1941, and the Soviet secret police take fifteen-year-old Lina, her mother and her brother from their home in Lithuania to a labor camp in Siberia. Lina draws everything she sees, hoping the pictures will reach her father.

title: In the Shadow of Blackbirds
author: Cat Winters
maturity_note: Wartime trauma, flu deaths and ghostly scares. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: San Diego, 1918, with the flu killing thousands and spirit photographers selling pictures of the dead. Sixteen-year-old Mary Shelley Black has a near-death experience, and her first love, killed in the war, starts visiting her. She sets out to find out what really happened to him.

title: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
author: Becky Albertalli
maturity_note: Some swearing, teen drinking and kissing. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Simon hasn't come out yet, and he's been emailing with an anonymous boy at his school who calls himself Blue. When a classmate finds the emails, he uses them to blackmail Simon. Funny, with a mystery at its center: who is Blue?

title: Darius the Great Is Not Okay
author: Adib Khorram
maturity_note: Depression and a dying grandfather; very little else. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: Darius is a Star Trek fan with depression who never feels Persian enough or American enough. His family travels to Iran for the first time to see his dying grandfather, and he makes his first real friend.

title: Children of Blood and Bone
author: Tomi Adeyemi
maturity_note: Lots of violence and some deaths. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: In Orïsha, the king wiped out magic and killed the people who used it. Zélie teams up with a runaway princess to bring magic back, while the crown prince hunts them. Fast, big and the first of a series.

title: Ace of Spades
author: Faridah Àbíké-Íyímídé
maturity_note: A sex tape, a girl strangled, two boys beaten after being seen kissing, an execution, the N-word, drinking and swearing. Common Sense Media: 16+.
description: Devon and Chiamaka are the only two Black students at an elite private school, and both have just been named senior prefects. Then an anonymous texter starts exposing their secrets, and it's bigger than bullying. A school thriller with a dark twist.

title: The Life and Crimes of Hoodie Rosen
author: Isaac Blum
maturity_note: Antisemitic threats and an attack, but no graphic violence. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Hoodie's Orthodox Jewish community has moved to a new town that doesn't want them. Then he falls for the mayor's daughter, whose mother is trying to keep them out. Funny, until the threats start getting serious.

title: Dear Martin
author: Nic Stone
maturity_note: Swearing, police violence and a shooting. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Justyce is a top student at a prep school, headed for the Ivy League, when a police officer handcuffs him for nothing. He starts writing letters to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. to work out how to live by his ideas. Then something worse happens.

title: Rez Ball
author: Byron Graves
maturity_note: Grief, some racism from opposing fans, and mild language. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Tre takes his late brother's place on the Red Lake Warriors, the basketball team his reservation lives for. Now he has to carry the team, and the town, toward a state title. A sports novel by an Ojibwe author.

title: The Inheritance Games
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
maturity_note: A shooting, bruises from an abusive relationship, and an explosion; a little romance. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Avery is barely getting by when a billionaire she's never met leaves her almost his entire fortune. To keep it she has to live in his mansion with the family he cut out, including four grandsons, and solve the puzzles he left behind.

title: The Cousins
author: Karen M. McManus
maturity_note: A few deaths in the family's past, some drinking, and frequent f-words. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Three cousins who barely know each other are invited to work a summer at their rich grandmother's island resort, though she disowned their parents years ago. Nobody will say why. The secret is worse than they think.

title: Death at Morning House
author: Maureen Johnson
maturity_note: Two deaths in the 1930s and a recent drowning; mild language and a little romance. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: After an embarrassing disaster, Marlowe takes a summer job giving tours of Morning House, an island mansion where two teenagers died in 1932. Then she learns she's replacing a guide who drowned. The story switches between her summer and what really happened in 1932.

title: The Red Palace
author: June Hur
maturity_note: Several murders, a cruel crown prince, some violence. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Korea, 1758. Hyeon is a palace nurse, and when four women are murdered in a single night, her mentor is arrested for it. To clear her, Hyeon teams up with a young police inspector, and the trail leads toward the crown prince himself.

title: Girl Forgotten
author: April Henry
maturity_note: A teenage girl's murder, drug addiction and an overdose, two deaths that may be suicides, and threats against the narrator. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Piper is a true-crime fan who starts a podcast about Layla Trello, a girl murdered seventeen years ago whose case was never solved. As the episodes get attention, someone starts warning her to stop. Told partly through podcast transcripts.

title: 49 Miles Alone
author: Natalie D. Richards
maturity_note: Danger in the wilderness, a possibly violent boyfriend, and a traumatic night in the cousins' past. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Two cousins are hiking the Utah backcountry when they meet a couple who seem off. That night the girl runs into the dark with her boyfriend chasing her, and by morning their camp is empty. By the author of Five Total Strangers.

title: The Girls I've Been
author: Tess Sharpe
maturity_note: Past sexual abuse by a con-man stepfather, including of a child (implied, not described); people shot, stabbed and burned during the robbery; frequent f-words. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Nora's mother was a con artist, and Nora spent her childhood pretending to be other girls. Now she's caught in a bank robbery with her ex-girlfriend and her current boyfriend, and her old skills are the only way out. Twisty and very fast.

title: Girl in the Blue Coat
author: Monica Hesse
maturity_note: Nazi occupation, deaths of loved ones, danger to Jewish families in hiding. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Amsterdam, 1943. Hanneke delivers black-market goods under the Nazis' noses. A customer begs her to find a Jewish girl in a blue coat who vanished from a hidden room. A mystery and a war story in one.

title: Catfishing on CatNet
author: Naomi Kritzer
maturity_note: A dangerous parent tracking his family; some peril. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Steph and her mother keep moving to hide from her father, so her only real friends are online, and her best friend there is a chatty AI that loves cat pictures. When her past catches up with her, the AI may be the only one who can help.

title: Patron Saints of Nothing
author: Randy Ribay
awards: National Book Award finalist 2019 · Edgar YA nominee 2020
maturity_note: Drug-war killings and photos of gruesome murders, a character sold into sex trafficking, drug use, some swearing. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Jay is a Filipino-American senior coasting toward college when he learns his cousin was killed in the Philippines' drug war. Nobody in the family will talk about it, so he flies there to find out what happened.

title: Sadie
author: Courtney Summers
maturity_note: Child sexual abuse is central (not shown), drug addiction, attempted rapes, a murder, violence and strong language. Common Sense Media: 16+.
description: Sadie's little sister was murdered, and Sadie has gone after the man she thinks did it. The story alternates between her road trip and a true-crime podcast trying to find her afterward. Gripping and very dark.

title: The Name of the Star
author: Maureen Johnson
maturity_note: Copycat Jack the Ripper murders, some described; mild romance. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Rory moves from Louisiana to a London boarding school just as someone starts copying Jack the Ripper's murders. She sees a man near one crime scene whom nobody else can see. Funny narrator, creepy mystery.

title: Shelter
author: Harlan Coben
maturity_note: Fairly violent: a brutal beating, a villain shot in the head, and a strip club tied to a trafficking ring. His mother is in drug rehab. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Mickey has just moved to a new town when his new girlfriend, Ashley, disappears without a trace. The deeper he digs, the more it connects to his own father's death. A fast thriller by a big-name adult mystery writer.

title: Paper Towns
author: John Green
maturity_note: Teens find a dead body (a suicide, described); swearing, drinking, references to masturbation and oral sex, and a near sex scene. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Quentin has loved his neighbor Margo since they were kids. One night she climbs through his window and takes him on an all-night revenge mission, and the next day she's gone, leaving clues that only he seems meant to follow.

title: Bog Child
author: Siobhan Dowd
maturity_note: Political violence and hunger strikes in Northern Ireland; a little romance. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Northern Ireland, 1981. Fergus is digging for peat when he finds the body of a child who died two thousand years ago. Meanwhile his brother is on hunger strike in prison and Fergus is being pulled into running mysterious packages across the border.

title: The Body of Christopher Creed
author: Carol Plum-Ucci
maturity_note: Bullying, a possible suicide or murder, some swearing. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Christopher Creed was the weird kid everyone picked on, and then one day he disappeared, leaving a strange note. Torey, who is popular, starts to wonder what part he played. The question is whether Chris ran away, killed himself, or was killed.

title: Silent to the Bone
author: E. L. Konigsburg
maturity_note: A baby is badly hurt; a manipulative au pair and some sexual undertones. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: Branwell's baby sister is badly hurt, and Branwell, who called 911, hasn't said a word since. His best friend Connor is the only one who believes he's innocent, and he sets out to get the truth out of him. By the author of From the Mixed-Up Files.

title: Acceleration
author: Graham McNamee
maturity_note: A would-be serial killer's diary describes killing animals and planning to kill women. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Duncan is stuck working in the Toronto subway's lost-and-found when he finds a diary written by someone planning to become a serial killer. The police won't listen, so Duncan and his friends go looking for him. Short and very tense.

title: What I Saw and How I Lied
author: Judy Blundell
maturity_note: A death and antisemitism; the 15-year-old narrator and an older man nearly have sex, and she starts to with a boy before stopping; heavy drinking and smoking. Common Sense Media: 15+.
description: 1947. Evie's stepfather is back from the war, and the family takes a sudden trip to Palm Beach, where Evie falls for a handsome young veteran. Then a hurricane hits, someone dies, and Evie has to decide what she saw and what she'll say.

title: Feed
author: M. T. Anderson
maturity_note: Constant swearing, some drinking, a serious illness. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Titus and his friends have the internet wired directly into their brains, and ads follow every thought. On a spring-break trip to the moon, a hacker scrambles their feeds, and Titus meets Violet, who is trying to resist it. A satire that feels more real every year.

title: The Absolutely True Diary of a Part-Time Indian
author: Sherman Alexie
maturity_note: Crude humor including masturbation jokes, alcoholism, several deaths, slurs. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Junior is a cartoonist growing up on the Spokane reservation, and he decides to transfer to the all-white high school in the farm town nearby. Everyone at home calls him a traitor. Told with his cartoons, it's very funny and very sad.

title: Challenger Deep
author: Neal Shusterman
maturity_note: Serious mental illness, a psychiatric hospital, and a suicide attempt; little language or sex. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Caden is a high school student who is starting to lose his grip on reality. In his mind he's also aboard a ship headed for the deepest point in the ocean. The two stories run side by side. Based on the author's son's experience.

title: The Graveyard Book
author: Neil Gaiman
maturity_note: A family is murdered in the opening pages (not graphic); ghosts and menace. Common Sense Media: 9+.
description: A toddler wanders into a graveyard on the night his family is murdered, and the ghosts decide to raise him. Bod grows up learning ghostly tricks, but the man who killed his family is still looking for him.

title: When You Reach Me
author: Rebecca Stead
maturity_note: A man is hit by a truck and killed in front of the narrator; a boy is punched. Common Sense Media: 9+.
description: New York, 1979. Twelve-year-old Miranda starts finding notes that predict things before they happen, and one says it's trying to save a life. Her favorite book is A Wrinkle in Time, which turns out to matter. A short puzzle that clicks at the end.

title: The Last Cuentista
author: Donna Barba Higuera
maturity_note: Earth is destroyed; a sinister group erases people's memories. Common Sense Media: 10+.
description: A comet is about to hit Earth, and Petra is one of a few people put to sleep on a ship to a new planet. When she wakes up centuries later, everyone else has been reprogrammed to forget Earth. Only Petra remembers, and she still has her grandmother's stories.

title: The Giver
author: Lois Lowry
maturity_note: A disturbing scene involving a baby; nothing graphic. Common Sense Media: 11+.
description: In Jonas's community there's no pain, no war and no choices, and at twelve everyone is assigned a job. Jonas is chosen to receive the memories of the past from an old man called the Giver, and he starts to see what has been taken away.

title: The Wednesday Wars
author: Gary D. Schmidt
maturity_note: Talk of the Vietnam War; a sister runs away. Common Sense Media: 10+.
description: 1967. Holling is the only kid in his class who doesn't leave for religious school on Wednesday afternoons, so he's stuck with Mrs. Baker, who he's sure hates him. She makes him read Shakespeare. It's much funnier than that sounds.

title: The War That Saved My Life
author: Kimberly Brubaker Bradley
maturity_note: An abusive mother and wartime bombing. Common Sense Media: 9+.
description: Ada has never left her London apartment because her mother is ashamed of her twisted foot. When children are evacuated before the Nazi bombing starts, Ada sneaks out with her brother and ends up in the countryside, learning to ride a horse and to trust someone.

title: A Monster Calls
author: Patrick Ness
maturity_note: A mother dying of cancer; bullying and one violent outburst. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: Conor's mother is sick, and every night a monster made from the yew tree outside comes to tell him stories. It wants something from him in return: the truth about his nightmare. Short, with an ending that will wreck you.

title: Salt to the Sea
author: Ruta Sepetys
maturity_note: Wartime deaths, a ship sinking, and a pregnancy from rape (not described). Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: 1945. Four teenagers fleeing the advancing Soviet army across East Prussia head for the ship that's supposed to save them, the Wilhelm Gustloff. Each has a secret. Based on the deadliest shipwreck in history.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
maturity_note: Animals are executed and worked to death, told plainly and without gore. Common Sense Media: 11+.
description: The animals of Manor Farm drive out their drunken farmer and set up a society where all animals are equal. Then the pigs start making the rules. Short, sharp, and funnier than its reputation.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
maturity_note: Ten deaths, including a suicide, none described graphically. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: Ten strangers are lured to an island mansion, and a voice accuses each of them of murder. Then they start dying, one by one, exactly as an old nursery rhyme predicts. The best-selling mystery ever written, and the original locked-island puzzle.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
maturity_note: One stabbing, off the page. The backstory involves a child's kidnapping and murder. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: A snowdrift stops a luxury train in the mountains, and in the morning a passenger is found stabbed twelve times. Hercule Poirot has a carriage full of suspects and no way out. The ending is one of the most famous twists in crime fiction.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
maturity_note: A few deaths and a menacing animal; nothing graphic. Common Sense Media: 10+.
description: A family legend says a demonic hound hunts the heirs of Baskerville Hall, and the latest heir has just arrived on the foggy moor. Sherlock Holmes sends Watson ahead to watch. The best of the Holmes novels and a good first one.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
maturity_note: A murder and an affair, discussed rather than shown. Builds slowly on dread. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: A shy young woman marries a wealthy widower and moves into his grand house, where his first wife, Rebecca, still seems to rule every room. The housekeeper makes sure she knows it. A gothic suspense novel with a twist that changes everything you've read.

title: The Daughter of Time
author: Josephine Tey
maturity_note: Nothing notable. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: A detective stuck in a hospital bed gets bored and decides to solve a crime nearly 500 years old: did Richard III really murder his nephews in the Tower? Working only from books and a helpful researcher, he takes the case apart. Often voted the best crime novel ever written.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
maturity_note: A woman chooses to burn with her books, a man is killed with a flamethrower, and a suicide attempt by overdose. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Guy Montag is a fireman, and in his world firemen burn books. Then a strange teenage neighbor asks him if he's happy, and he starts secretly keeping one. Short and urgent.

title: Ender's Game
author: Orson Scott Card
maturity_note: Kids fight and two are killed, some graphically; frequent crude language, including racial and antisemitic slurs. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: Earth is training gifted children to fight an alien invasion, and six-year-old Ender Wiggin may be the commander they've been waiting for. Battle School is a zero-gravity war game, and the adults are rigging it against him. The ending is famous for a reason.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
maturity_note: A rape trial at the center (not shown), racial slurs throughout, and an attack on two children. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: In 1930s Alabama, Scout Finch's father defends a Black man falsely accused of attacking a white woman. Scout tells it as she lived it, with a mysterious neighbor named Boo Radley in the background. Funny and warm until it isn't.

title: Flowers for Algernon
author: Daniel Keyes
maturity_note: Some sexual content and frank talk about sex; cruelty toward a disabled man. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Charlie Gordon has an IQ of 68 until an experimental surgery makes him a genius. He tells the story in his own progress reports, and you watch his spelling, and his understanding of the people around him, change. It will make you cry.

title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
author: Mark Haddon
maturity_note: Frequent strong language, including f-words. A parent's affair is at the center of the plot. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Fifteen-year-old Christopher, who loves math and hates being touched, finds a neighbor's dog killed with a garden fork and decides to investigate like Sherlock Holmes. What he uncovers is about his own family. Told in his voice, with diagrams.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
maturity_note: Constant swearing and little else. A classroom edition removes the profanity. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: An astronaut is left for dead on Mars with a broken habitat and food for a fraction of the time until rescue could possibly arrive. So he starts solving problems, one at a time, with science and a lot of jokes. Pure momentum.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
maturity_note: A few f-words, characters discuss how they'd end their lives if the mission fails, and life-or-death danger. Common Sense Media: 14+.
description: A man wakes up alone on a spaceship with no memory of who he is or why he's there. Slowly he remembers: he's the last hope to save Earth from a dying sun. Then he finds out he isn't alone.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
maturity_note: One death and a menacing villain; nothing graphic. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Piranesi lives in a vast house of endless halls filled with statues, where the tides flood the lower floors. He believes only one other person is alive. His own journal entries slowly reveal that he's wrong about almost everything.

title: Station Eleven
author: Emily St. John Mandel
maturity_note: A pandemic kills most people; a cult leader takes child brides (not shown); some violence. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: A flu wipes out most of humanity, and twenty years later a troupe of actors and musicians travels the Great Lakes performing Shakespeare. A strange comic book and a dangerous prophet connect their story to the world before. Hopeful more than grim.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
maturity_note: Frank and unromantic sexual content between teenagers; a quietly devastating premise. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: Kathy remembers growing up at Hailsham, an English boarding school where the students were told they were special. Slowly, through her memories, you learn what they were being raised for. Quiet, sad, and impossible to forget.

author: George Orwell
maturity_note: Long torture scenes, a sexual relationship with some sex described, and an unrelentingly brutal world. Common Sense Media: 16+.
description: Winston Smith works at the Ministry of Truth, rewriting history so the Party is always right. Big Brother is watching, and even thinking the wrong thing is a crime. Winston starts keeping a diary anyway.

title: Lord of the Flies
author: William Golding
maturity_note: Boys hunt and kill other boys; brutal by the end. Common Sense Media: 12+.
description: A plane full of schoolboys crashes on a deserted island, and with no adults they try to govern themselves. It goes well for about a chapter. A grim, gripping story about what people are like underneath.

title: The Princess Bride
author: William Goldman
maturity_note: Sword fights and a torture machine played mostly for laughs. Common Sense Media: 10+.
description: Fencing, fighting, torture, revenge, giants, monsters, chases, escapes, true love, and miracles. The author pretends to be abridging an older book and keeps interrupting with jokes. Different from the movie in good ways.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
maturity_note: Battles and a dragon; nothing graphic. Common Sense Media: 9+.
description: Bilbo Baggins likes his quiet hole in the ground until a wizard and thirteen dwarves show up and drag him off to steal treasure from a dragon. Riddles in the dark, giant spiders, and one very important ring.

title: Of Mice and Men
author: John Steinbeck
maturity_note: Racial slurs, a killing, and a mercy killing at the end. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: George and Lennie are migrant ranch hands in Depression-era California, saving up for a farm of their own. Lennie is enormous, gentle, and doesn't know his own strength. Very short and very sad.

title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
author: Shirley Jackson
maturity_note: Most of a family was poisoned years ago, and the town turns violent toward the survivors. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Eighteen-year-old Merricat lives in a big house with her sister and her uncle. The rest of the family died of arsenic at dinner six years ago, and the village hates them for it. Merricat narrates, and she is not quite right.

title: The Haunting of Hill House
author: Shirley Jackson
maturity_note: Psychological scares rather than gore; one death. No Common Sense Media rating; this score is Claude's estimate.
description: Four people move into a notorious mansion to study whether it's haunted. The house seems especially interested in Eleanor, the lonely one. The classic haunted-house novel, scarier for what it doesn't show.

title: The Night Circus
author: Erin Morgenstern
maturity_note: One character is stabbed to death and another steps in front of a train; one f-word; a little romance. Common Sense Media: 15+.
description: A black-and-white circus appears without warning and is open only at night. Behind it, two young magicians are bound to a contest neither fully understands, and the circus is their battlefield. Lush and dreamlike.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
maturity_note: Childhood cruelty, a fire, and a dark secret in the attic. Common Sense Media: 13+.
description: An orphan survives a cruel aunt and a crueler school, then becomes governess at Thornfield Hall, where strange laughter comes from the third floor. She falls for its moody owner anyway. A gothic romance with a heroine who refuses to be pushed around.
